How many tokens does one source cover, across the band and the sky?

Each point is one prior source (four per window). The span is the tokens touched by the central 99% (or 90%) of its SNR²; "fewest" counts only the tokens needed to hold that share. The line is the analytic span at the ecliptic plane (|cos β| = 1) with ḟ 5σ above the prior's mean at f0: 2 × (Doppler + drift + antenna sidebands) bins.

Count

Does the analytic Doppler band predict the measured span?

Measured central-99% width against 2 × (f0 v/c |cos β| T + Ḟ T² + 4 T/yr) bins, β the ecliptic latitude. On the line the analytic band is the 99% width.

How concentrated is a source's power?

Share of a source's SNR² in the token holding f0, and in its loudest token, as cumulative fractions of sources.

What this means

  • A source is a few tokens, not one. Its central 99% of SNR² spans a median 3 tokens on both bands (5–95%: 2–4 and 2–5, at most 4 and 7). The span grows with f0: a median 3 tokens (27 bins) below 1.5 mHz, 4 tokens (54 bins) above 3 mHz (full only). Narrow sources sit at 0.82–2.97 mHz.
  • The token holding f0 carries little more than half the power. It holds a median 60% of SNR² on narrow and 57% on full, and 13% (narrow) and 29% (full) of sources keep less than half there.
  • The sky barely changes the span under this prior. The sources' sky prior puts them near the ecliptic, so |cos β| has median 0.989 and the Doppler band is nearly at its maximum for almost every source. Span varies with f0, not with sky position.
  • The analytic band is slightly wide. The measured 99% width is 0.77–0.93 (narrow) and 0.78–0.94 (full) of 2 × (Doppler + drift + 4 T/yr) at 5–95%, median 0.86 for both; the extremes are 0.64–1.33 and 0.66–1.99.
  • The guard holds real signal for some sources. More than 1% of SNR² falls in a guard token for 16% of narrow sources (up to 55%) and 10% of full sources (up to 55%).
